vulnerability_analysis: The JizzJet contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the swapAndLiquify function. When contract token balance exceeds numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity threshold (100000000 * 10^10), any transfer triggers swapAndLiquify. This function calls swapTokensForEth which interacts with Uniswap router, then sendBNBToAdmin transfers ETH to _adminWalletAddress. The vulnerability allows reentrancy during the external Uniswap call, and if _adminWalletAddress is a malicious contract, it can capture ETH during the transfer.
attack_strategy: 1) Deploy a malicious contract with receive/fallback to capture ETH. 2) Inject tokens and transfer them to the victim contract to accumulate balance above threshold. 3) Trigger a transfer that causes swapAndLiquify execution. 4) During the swap/transfer process, the malicious admin wallet (if we can set it) or reentrancy during Uniswap call allows ETH extraction. 5) Verify attacker balance increased.
step_by_step_plan: 1) Create malicious contract with receive() to capture ETH. 2) Use deal() to get native tokens for gas. 3) Inject JizzJet tokens to attacker. 4) Transfer tokens to victim contract to build up balance above numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity. 5) Trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring more tokens. 6) Capture ETH sent to admin wallet or during reentrancy. 7) Assert attacker balance increased.
